feat\(worksheet\): 3-level progressive hints with score penalty

Worksheet cell hint modal \(?\) no longer reveals the numeric answer.
Each yellow cell now exposes 3 progressively concrete hints —
L1 conceptual → L2 mechanism → L3 formula — and the cell'"'"'s grading
weight scales down with the highest level used:

  HINT_PENALTY = [1.0, 0.7, 0.4, 0.2]  \(idx = level 0..3\)

Wrong answers always score 0; the penalty only applies on correct
cells. The grading panel reports both the raw count and the weighted
score \(e.g., "4.1 / 6 \(정답 5/6 · 힌트 차감 −0.9\)"\). A yellow H1/H2/H3
badge is rendered on cells whose hints were viewed.

To make the trade-off explicit and visible, the modal shows the
current and next-step rate \("배점 70% → 40%"\), and a banner above
the worksheet states the policy before any hint is requested.

Hint copy across all 4 cases \(01-loading, 04-material-yield,
05-cuts-mask, 06-tact-investment\) deliberately stops short of
computing the answer — only the formula and substitution path are
shown at L3.

Constraint: hints must not reveal answer numbers at any level
Constraint: existing legacy `hint` field preserved for AI coach context
Rejected: separate hint button per level | UI clutter on small cells
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Directive: HINT_PENALTY weights are pedagogically tuned — coordinate
with instructor before changing.

EOF
